QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_45

question.text: Which of the following best describes the 'Liquidation Period' under Regulation 29(9A)?

answer.text: A 2-year period before scheme launch for capital-raising
A 1-year period following expiry of tenure (or extended tenure) of the AIF scheme, for fully liquidating scheme assets
A perpetual period with unlimited extension
A 6-month period immediately after scheme launch

explanation.text: The Logic: The 'Liquidation Period' is a period of 1 year following the expiry of tenure or extended tenure of the AIF scheme, during which the manager fully liquidates scheme assets. Where assets cannot be liquidated within that window, in-specie distribution or entry into the Dissolution Period (with 75% investor consent) is the route forward. The Trap: Options A, C and D invert the purpose or timing of the Liquidation Period. The 1-year post-tenure definition is the prescribed rule. Note: The Liquidation Period definition is on workbook p. 357; if the scheme intends to enter the Dissolution Period, the merchant-banker filing (Information Memorandum + Due-Diligence Certificate) must be made before the Liquidation Period expires (p. 359).
